title: Headcount scenarios + 1:1 prep (Diego)
content:
Purpose:
- Quick prep for upcoming 1:1 with Maya (hiring manager) and weekly headcount sync.
- Surface 3 realistic headcount scenarios, shortlist interview-loop fixes, and draft debrief/action checklist so we can move from talk -> decision in the same meeting.

Audience:
- Hiring manager, recruiter, people ops lead (triage).

Goals for the 1:1:
- Align on hiring priority rank (A/B/C) and acceptable delay window per role.
- Agree one immediate experiment to reduce interviewer overhead this week.
- Lock owner + due date for ramp / offer cadence changes.

Quick numbers (current funnel - snapshot):
- Req count open: 8 (2 SWE infra, 1 infra manager, 2 SWE infra (senior), 1 QA, 2 PM)
- Active candidates in pipeline: 42 (phone screen: 15, onsites: 6, offers in flight: 3)
- Avg time-to-offer: 37 days (target 28)
- Interviewer coverage: 12 ppl doing screens, avg load 6 screens/week
- No-show rate: 12% last 30 days

Three headcount scenarios (short, medium, long):
- Scenario A (Aggressive): Hire all 8 over next 10 weeks. Assumes 20% faster interview throughput, +2 dedicated interviewers (contract), and 2x offer acceptance rate improvements. Risk: high spend and burn on bench, interview capacity misses.
- Scenario B (Staggered - recommended): Prioritize top 4 reqs (2 infra eng, infra manager, PM) over 12 weeks, freeze remaining 4 for 6 weeks. Use rotating interviewer pool + reduced onsite to 1-day loop. Lower risk, keeps runway.
- Scenario C (Conservative): Hire 2 critical roles now (infra manager + senior SWE) and re-evaluate in 10 weeks. Focus on quality and cost control.

Interview loop adjustments to propose (fast experiments):
1) Trim early screen from 30m -> 20m for clear-fit candidates (saves ~25% interviewer time).
2) Implement a rotating "no-show buffer" slot each day for reschedules (reduces backlog).
3) Pair phonescreens with quick take-home assignment for senior ICs to reduce onsite time.
4) Interviewer fatigue: limit consecutive interviews to 3/half-day; track "interviewer index" in weekly sheet.

Debrief template (use in debrief doc & Slack post-onsite):
- Candidate name | role | stage | summary (1-2 sentences) | strengths (bullets) | risks (bullets) | score 1-5 (skills) | score 1-5 (team fit) | recommended next step
- Quick rule: if any interviewer flags 'critical miss', auto no-offer unless mitigations identified.

Decision heuristics (for the meeting):
- If offers in flight >=2 and acceptance probability <50% -> hold new reqs unless role is critical.
- If time-to-offer > 30d for a role with high priority -> escalate to hiring manager to add interviewers or remove onsite step.

Prep notes to bring to 1:1:
- Current offer acceptance reasons from last 6 hires (beatsheet).
- List of 3 internal engineers who can be short-term interview capacity if needed.
- Rough budget impact of scenario A vs B over next 3 months (high-level).

Draft script for hiring manager ask (30s):
- "Maya — two choices for next 12 weeks: aggressive fill of 8 or staggered focus on the top 4. I recommend staggered (B) to keep runway and lower interviewer burnout. Need your call today plus one interviewer add (or -> contract) to hit the 12-week timeline. Can you confirm preference?"

Action items (owner / due):
- Diego: pull acceptance reasons + last 6 offer debriefs (due 2026-03-14).
- Aisha: draft revised phone screen template (20m) and share sample questions (due 2026-03-13).
- Noah: propose two engineers for interview coverage (due 2026-03-13).
- Maya: decide scenario A/B/C in 1:1 (meeting date 2026-03-15).
- People Ops: update headcount tracker after decision and create a simple heatmap for risk (due 2026-03-16).

Open questions to resolve in meeting:
- What is the minimum hiring velocity we need to hit product roadmap milestones?
- Any upcoming events (conferences, holidays) that will materially affect interviewer availability in April?

Notes-to-self
- Keep conversation short and data-driven; avoid rehashing past disagreements.
- If Maya pushes for aggressive fill, push back with clear runway and bench-cost numbers.
- Be ready to propose a pilot: 2-week experiment to cut phone screen time + add buffer slot; measure impact and report at next sync.

Snippets (copy-paste)
- Candidate follow-up: "Thanks for taking the onsite — we'll share decision timeline by EOD Friday. If you have any questions in the meantime, reply here."
- Interviewer calibration prompt: "Please rate skills 1-5 and add one sentence justification. If you have a major concern, mark 'critical miss'."

Finish: want to leave meeting with 1) chosen scenario, 2) owned action list with dates, 3) small experiment running this week.

End of notes.
